write_authority: eravors_grammar — §10.1, the store only. The tab renders and confirms; it never writes.
failure_modes: no storage -> constructor throws, refuses to operate blind
term over 80 / meaning over 600 chars -> throws, naming the limit
proposing an existing live word -> throws, pointing at addMeaning/takeUp
taking up your OWN proposal -> throws; this is the structural guarantee
taking up a retired word -> throws, says propose it again first
unknown state on entries() -> throws, listing known states
unknown remote action -> throws, validated BEFORE the entry lookup so it cannot be swallowed
remote action about an unknown entry -> ignored quietly, returns null
invariants: TWO-SIDED BY CONSTRUCTION: proposed -> shared has exactly one path, takeUp(), and it refuses the proposer. No flag, argument or admin path bypasses it. Holds over the wire.
TWO MEANINGS, NEVER MERGED: no canonical meaning field exists. Divergence is reported, never resolved.
§0.3 meanings APPEND — a meaning drifting over years is kept, not overwritten
§0.3 retire and decline keep the entry; reviving returns it to PROPOSED, needing take-up afresh
§1.1 grammar is NEVER inferred. candidates() returns [] with a stated reason; health().inferred is structurally 0
retire is unilateral by design — taking a word up needs both, putting it down does not
§0.4 bounded at 400; retired entries are dropped before live ones
termsIn() matches SHARED terms only, on word boundaries — a proposal must never link two moments

lattice.why_not_folded_into_lexical: Two moments using the same SHARED word are related differently from two using the same ordinary word. Averaging them into one lexical score destroys exactly that distinction.
lattice.why_read_at_ingest: grammarTerms are resolved when the utterance is ingested, so a word taken up LATER does not retroactively rewrite history.
